newsitem.title: FRANCE: Consumer spending, working days help Q3 GDP-INSEE.
newsitem.headline: Consumer spending, working days help Q3 GDP-INSEE.

text.p: National statistics institute INSEE said on Thursday a favourable number of working days contributed 0.25 percentage point to GDP growth in the third quarter which rose 0.9 percent.
In the second quarter, the number of working days knocked off about half a point from GDP growth, it said.
Consumer spending, which rose one percent in the third quarter, contributed 0.6 percentage point to the GDP rise. Investment rose 1.0 percent, contributing 0.2 percentage point to growth.
Stocks variation contributed negatively to GDP by 0.3 percentage point, offset by a 0.3 percentage point positive contribution from trade.

The rise in household consumption was powered by spending on manufactured products which rose 2.7 percent after falling 1.7 percent in the previous quarter, INSEE said. Automobile spending was up 13.6 percent after falling 3.7 percent in the previous quarter. The third quarter rise was due to a rush to buy cars ahead of the September 30 expiry of a government subsidy scheme.

Buying of household equipment rose 1.4 percent after falling 2.4 percent in the previous quarter. Consumption of transport and telecommuncations rose 2.3 percent while spending on merchandise services grew 0.5 percent. Spending on food fell 0.2 percent.
INSEE also said a 2.7 percent rise in investment by non-financial businesses was boosted by a 3.4 percent increase in spending on manufactured products.
It said this rise was driven chiefly by investment in capital goods and to a lesser extent by investment in car production and metals.
